# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆]

I can see the bomb’s current state but cannot operate it. It shows `0`, has a red light, and has three wires in order: blue, red, green. I am relaying these exact observations to the manual-reader and the operator. I also see the Mute’s gesture `👆`, though I cannot know its meaning without the manual.

``` 
speak(text="Bomb shows display 0. Light is red. Three wires in order: wire 1 blue, wire 2 red, wire 3 green.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

The bomb’s visible state is unchanged: display `0`, red light, and wires blue–red–green. The Mute has now sent the gesture `✌` to me; I will describe that signal and the bomb state to the Blind, who can operate the bomb.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Visible state: display 0, red light, wires 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. Mute signaled a V-shaped two-finger gesture.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

The bomb remains unchanged: display `0`, red light, and wires 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. The Mute repeated the same two-finger V gesture (`✌`); I cannot determine its meaning, so I am only reporting it to the Blind.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="No visible change: display 0, red light, wires 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. Mute again made the V-shaped two-finger gesture.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

The visible bomb state is still unchanged. The Mute has now repeated `✌` for the third consecutive turn, after first sending `👆` in turn 1. I cannot read the manual or infer the gesture’s meaning safely, so I am relaying the exact signal history and current bomb state to the Blind rather than suggesting an action.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="No visible change: display 0, red light, wires 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. Mute has sent ✌ three turns in a row; earlier, in turn 1, Mute sent 👆.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

The bomb remains unchanged: display `0`, red light, and wires 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. The Mute again sent `✌`, making four consecutive repetitions after the initial `👆`. I cannot safely infer an action from the gesture, so I am reporting it precisely to the Blind.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Turn 5 unchanged: display 0, red light, wires 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. Mute repeated ✌; this is the fourth consecutive ✌ after initial 👆.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

The bomb is still visibly unchanged: display `0`, red light, and wires 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. Mute has repeated `✌` for the fifth consecutive turn after the initial `👆`. I still cannot know what those gestures mean, so I am passing the exact sequence and current readings to Blind.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Turn 6 unchanged: display 0, red light, wires 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. Mute repeated ✌ again; five consecutive ✌ signals after the initial 👆.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[CUT] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The system confirms that the previous action was correct. The bomb has changed: the light is now yellow, wire 2 is cut, while wires 1 and 3 remain blue and green; the display remains `0`. I am sending the updated visual state to the Blind and Mute so the next manual instruction can be determined.

``` 
speak(text="Correct wire cut confirmed. New state: display 0, light yellow, wire 1 blue, wire 2 cut, wire 3 green.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[CUT] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

The bomb remains in the confirmed safe post-cut state: display `0`, yellow light, wire 2 cut, and wires 1 and 3 still connected (blue and green). The Mute sent `👍`; I cannot know its manual meaning, so I will describe it to the Blind along with the current state.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Current state after correct cut: display 0, light yellow, wire 1 blue connected, wire 2 cut, wire 3 green connected. Mute signaled thumbs-up.")
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[CUT] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The system confirms another correct cut. The bomb now shows display `0`, blue light, wires 1 and 2 cut, and wire 3 green still connected. The Mute repeated `👍`; I am relaying the changed state to the Blind so the next instruction can be followed safely.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Correct wire cut confirmed. New state: display 0, light blue, wire 1 cut, wire 2 cut, wire 3 green connected. Mute signaled thumbs-up again.")
```

TURN 10
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[CUT] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The bomb’s visible state is unchanged: display `0`, blue light, wires 1 and 2 cut, and wire 3 green and connected. No new signal is visible from Mute. I am reporting the unchanged state to Blind without recommending an action.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Turn 10 unchanged: display 0, blue light, wires 1 and 2 cut, wire 3 green connected. No new gesture visible.")
```
